findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Treasury Management Report Quarter 1 2026-27
findings.headline: The council generated net positive interest income of £0.666 million in Q1 2026-27, with £0.704 million investment income offsetting borrowing costs.
findings.detail: For the period 1 April to 30 June 2026, interest received on £68m of treasury investments exceeded interest paid on £94.53m of borrowing. However, this favorable position is temporary and depends on deploying the large investment balance for capital expenditure and refinancing the LOBO debt at higher rates.
findings.matters: Current positive interest income is a favorable near-term position but masks that the council is a borrower; once reserves are deployed and LOBO debt is refinanced at 7.52%, the council will face material net borrowing costs.
findings.figures: £0.704 million interest income; net interest income £0.666 million for Q1 2026-27
findings.quote: The overall interest receivable from treasury investments for the period 1 April 2026 to 30 June 2026 was £0.704 million.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Treasury Management Report Quarter 1 2026-27
findings.headline: Average returns on treasury investments have fallen from 4.29% to 3.71%, as short-term loans to other local authorities matured at the end of the financial year.
findings.detail: The council holds £68m of treasury investments (up from £44.5m in the previous quarter) but the weighted average rate has declined. This reflects the maturity of higher-yielding short-term loans to other councils that had been placed at good rates over the year-end period, now reinvested at lower rates.
findings.matters: Declining investment returns reduce the council's cash generation capacity and indicate portfolio repositioning toward lower-yielding assets; this affects the council's net borrowing cost and cash interest income.
findings.figures: £68.00 million invested at 30 June 2026; average rate fell from 4.29% to 3.71%
findings.quote: Average interest rates on investments as at 30 June 2026 were 3.71%, a reduction from those at 31 March 2026 of 4.29%. This decrease is due to the maturity of several short term loans made to other Local Authorities (LAs) over the end of year period which had secured good interest rates.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Treasury Management Report Quarter 1 2026-27
findings.headline: The council's Capital Financing Requirement is growing, forecast to increase to £193.21 million by 31 March 2027 and £200.82 million by 31 March 2028.
findings.detail: Capital commitments in the approved capital programme are driving increases in the underlying debt funding requirement. Actual CFR at 31 March 2026 was £182.56m, with forecasts showing 5.8% growth in 2026-27 and further growth to £200.82m by 2028, on the assumption no new schemes are added.
findings.matters: A growing CFR indicates the council is committing to capital investment that will require external financing; it shows both the scale of capital ambition and the scale of future borrowing need.
findings.figures: CFR £182.56m (31 March 2026 actual), £193.21m (31 March 2027 forecast), £200.82m (31 March 2028 forecast)
findings.quote: The CFR is anticipated to increase in the next year assuming capital expenditure is incurred as currently anticipated.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Treasury Management Report Quarter 1 2026-27
findings.headline: The council is funding capital expenditure through internal borrowing (drawing down reserves) rather than external debt, with £69.97 million in use as of 31 March 2026.
findings.detail: Internal borrowing arises because the council's Capital Financing Requirement (£182.56m) exceeds external debt (£99.72m), with the £69.97m gap funded from temporary cash balances and reserves. The paper acknowledges this is prudent while reserves are available but that these will be replaced with external borrowing as reserves deplete.
findings.matters: Drawing down reserves to fund capital reduces the council's financial buffers and creates future refinancing pressure; a lender would be concerned about both the rate of reserve depletion and the council's plan to replace it.
findings.figures: £69.97 million internal borrowing; CFR £182.56 million at 31 March 2026; external debt £99.72 million
findings.quote: Internal borrowing was £69.97 million as at 31 March 2026. This is shown by the Council's Capital Financing Requirement (CFR) net of its external level of debt including other long term debt liabilities.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Treasury Management Report Quarter 1 2026-27
findings.headline: The council forecasts a need to borrow £70.58 million during 2026-27, including the £19.25 million LOBO refinancing.
findings.detail: The liability benchmark indicates the council may need to borrow £70.58m in 2026-27 to fund capital expenditure and replace maturing debt, with the LOBO repayment representing 27% of this total. The paper notes this figure is likely to reduce as capital expenditure and reserve usage forecasts are updated through the year.
findings.matters: A borrowing requirement of this scale indicates material ongoing refinancing needs and tight cash management; a lender would need to understand whether replacement funding has been committed.
findings.figures: £70.58 million forecast borrowing need; £19.25 million LOBO component
findings.quote: the forecast need to borrow during the year is £70.58 million, although this is likely to reduce as capital expenditure and use of earmarked reserves forecasts are updated during the year. This figure includes the repayment of the LOBO loans of £ 19.25 million, which may need to be refinanced either in total or in part duing the year.
